I'm happy to help some with the review log. Question: @Will Blair created a review skill in FC#4899. Would it be helpful to use/experiment with this skill?
That sounds great @Bo Cowgill ! I think experimenting with it would be very useful. I'll probably review and merge FC#4899 shortly so others can use it easily

Following this invitation, I’ve completed a first batch of reviews and trialled the review skill, including on FC#4405. The reviews are posted, but GitHub still reports “review required.” Just confirming: is this the expected behavior, and are reviews from contributors without write access still useful for the final review and merge process?

Bo Cowgill said:

The reviews are posted, but GitHub still reports “review required.” Just confirming: is this the expected behavior, and are reviews from contributors without write access still useful for the final review and merge process?

I think GitHub still reporting "review required" might be because the review was posted as a comment - I don't thing this is an issue at all! When merging PRs, I find reviewers from other contributors very helpful and absolutely take those into account
(and feel free to ping me on PRs you've reviewed and think are ready to merge!)

thanks @Bo Cowgill !
The first batch looks reasonable. Indepently of the review skill that is used, I think it is quite important to make sure to use a fairly capable AI agent and it would be useful information in the review what model was used, mainly to also adjust priors on what those models catch

regarding "2." in the Outstanding tasks v1 list:
FC#6448 and FC#6591

I have created subissues for each of those, which should make it easier to work on those

@Moritz Firsching -- happy that the initial reviews looked good. I did some amount of manual review as well, although I agree it would be useful to state what AI was used. FWIW, I've been using GPT Sol 6.1 on xhigh. This is the recently released GPT version that's near Astra-levels, but more token-efficient. When necessary I have been using Astra xhigh -- it just burns through credits must faster and did not seem to be noticeably better for this type of work.

Ah yes, there are a few places with external repos coming up. Anyway -- thanks for the guidance and I'll get back to the backlog. Ping about anything else.

Also -- for ones that I suggest to approve, should I just leave them with a review that's "approved" and move on? Or do you want me to flag those? Happy to just leave them approved for whenever you get to them if that's the preference.
ah, flagging them would probably be helpful, yes, perhaps manually for now (for instance here or in some thread), but we can also get something like mathlib's "maintainer merge" going

Sure, here's a list of the ones I've reviewed. I basically spent all of yesterday on these so there are a bunch; I just wanted to gain some more experience. Feedback welcome.

Simple approvals

  • FC#4405 — Erdős 1052 proof links
  • FC#5165 — Repunit prime infinitude — newer revision since my approval.
  • FC#5166 — Euclid–Fortunate coverage
  • FC#5168 — Emirp infinitude
  • FC#5169 — Smarandache–Wellin primes
  • FC#5186 — Total colouring
  • FC#5190 — Alon–Saks–Seymour
  • FC#5195 — Sumner’s universal tournament conjecture

Approved with nonblocking documentation/citation requests

  • FC#4388 — Erdős 708 — documentation clarifications and a source-reference question.
  • FC#5188 — Seymour’s second neighbourhood conjecture — fix the Wikipedia link.
  • FC#5191 — Manickam–Miklós–Singhi — fix the Wikipedia link.
  • FC#5192 — Gyárfás–Sumner — qualify the path bound’s domain.
  • FC#5193 — Lovász’s conjecture — describe the dense variant as a Hamiltonian-path corollary.

Changes requested

  • FC#4370 — Erdős 667 — three corrections requested; a newer revision is available.
  • FC#5197 — Cycle double cover — the girth variant does not match its cited result.

Other / no approval submitted

  • FC#5189 — 1-2-3 conjecture — positive review submitted as “Comment”; attribution and link corrections requested.
  • FC#4470 — Erdős 349 positive result — submitted as “Comment”; requested pinned proof links and reproducible verification.
  • FC#5167 — Van Eck coverage — review completed and draft prepared, but not submitted.

one thing: to be more useful it sometimes help to be less verbose: typically there is no information in the fact that build --wfailpasses and what axioms are used, this is something that is already checked by the CI

Let me know if you see specific good "less verbosity" examples in the reviews. Some of the reviews are (arguably) too long, but some include additional outside courses consulted, exact page numbers, and/or any interpretation needed for the approval. Those seems useful to record, but I want to comply with the verbosity request. Let me know if you see any that seem like too much and I'll investigate and refine.

@Moritz Firsching, good to see some of the PRs I reviewed have merged. Before I take on another batch, any feedback on the recent reviews? What helped, and were there recurring gaps that came up in your follow-up checks?

@Bo Cowgill
Your reviews have been helpful and I have not seen any instance where they falsely flagged something as wrong.

The gaps were minor and I didn't spot a repeating pattern, I often only requested having a formal_proof link if possible, align with Mathlib naming and potentially moving stuff to ForMathlib

I was reviewing stuff that was fairly easy to review earlier today, many of which your review confirmed that the contribution was ok.

Thanks for the help!

Thanks @Moritz Firsching. Some authors have quickly addressed the review findings; others haven’t responded yet.

For PRs that remain inactive, would it make sense to prepare small fixes ourselves when the required changes are straightforward? We could open follow-up or replacement PRs, preserving the original author’s credit, so useful contributions can still move forward. Mathematical changes would still need independent review.
creating code suggestion and if there are uncontroversial also commiting them seems fine to me and I have been doing it

Moritz Firsching said:

creating code suggestion and if there are uncontroversial also commiting them seems fine to me and I have been doing it

Good to know, I don't have permissions to commit to other authors PRs so I'll hold off on that.

In my reviewing, comparator and external-proof verification have been really slow and resource-intensive. When it's ready, this project could be really useful:

"ix is a zero-knowledge proof-carrying code platform for Lean 4. Ix compiles Lean programs and proofs into succinct cryptographic certificates: instead of rechecking a formal proof, anyone can verify a small zk-SNARK attesting that the proof was checked."

We’d still need to confirm that the certified statement matches the conjecture.

Yeah it would be nice to have better infrastructure to easily check external proofs. Short term, the goal is to move towards requiring contributors to only use Palomar submissions when they are contributing links to formal proofs of research problems
